chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Fadl, Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The woman who pays khul' (compensation for divorce), if she returns to negotiate a part of the settlement, he says to her: 'I will return to you my right of conjugal access (to your body).'

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: The woman who pays khul' (compensation for divorce)
key_terms.بُضْعِكِ: Your conjugal access/body (right of the husband)

ai.seo_question: What happens if a woman seeks to reclaim part of her khul' compensation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the husband's right of retraction (*ruju'*) when a wife initiates *khul'* and subsequently seeks to reclaim part of the compensation. It establishes that the husband may assert his conjugal rights to validate the transaction or retain the settlement, reflecting the Shia juristic view that *khul'* is a mutual contract where the husband's consent is pivotal. This ruling underscores the balance of rights in divorce, ensuring the husband is not deprived of his marital authority without clear agreement.
